checks.title: Entry-timing difference is declared
checks.detail: kernel enters at the hourly close; the live bot scans every 5 min on a forming candle, so the kernel reads pumps +0.59pp larger on average (200 matched setups). DECLARED LIMITATION: arena absolute WR is not live WR. Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel — but a promoted arm must still survive the earlier live entry, and that caveat is attached to every surfaced verdict.

findings.claim: Checklist item paired_population is green with the detail 'Every arm scored on identical events — 4814 events in the shared window; every arm has seen all of them', and the arena header states 'all arms share identical detections'.
findings.problem: Seeing an event is not being scored on it. entry-8pct reports screen_n=496 and vol-4x screen_n=866 against control screen_n=1550, so any arm-vs-arm comparison involving them is run on different, self-selected subsets rather than a paired population. The same checklist's open-trade breakdown lists control, hold-12h, placebo, sl-5pct, tp-7pct and vol-4x but omits entry-8pct entirely, which is further evidence that arm is not inside the shared scoring table. A green 'identical events' box here overstates what the pairing guarantees.

findings.claim: entry-8pct is reported with screen_dWR=0.0pp and vol-4x with screen_dWR=0.0pp, the same delta-vs-control value carried by control itself and by the inert placebo.
findings.problem: Those two arms report screen_wr=51.613 and screen_wr=51.27 against control screen_wr=49.935 — different win rates cannot honestly carry a delta of 0.0pp versus that control. Either the delta is being suppressed because the samples are not paired (n=496 and n=866 versus n=1550), in which case the field should be blank rather than zero, or it is being computed wrongly. As printed, two arms are indistinguishable from the placebo in the only column that is supposed to express effect size, which is exactly the accounting artifact (ACC) failure mode this project lists.

findings.claim: 'measured ghost arrival = 25.2 control trades/day' is presented as the arrival rate used to reason about reaching the confirm sample of n=600.
findings.problem: The live tape does not show that rate anywhere. Control reports live_n=13, placebo live_n=13, hold-12h live_n=13, sl-5pct live_n=12, vol-4x live_n=7 and entry-8pct live_n=3, while events by tier gives live=50 against backfill=4764 over a 62.0-day data span. A rate of 25.2 control trades/day is irreconcilable with control having accumulated 13 live trades, so the arrival figure is either measured on backfill and mislabelled 'control trades/day', or it is stale. Any statement about time-to-n=600 that rests on it is unsupported.

findings.claim: Checklist item arms_running is green: '5 running: tp-7pct, hold-12h, entry-8pct, sl-5pct, vol-4x', treated as a critical pass.
findings.problem: The arena itself lists seven arms in running/confirm state — the five named plus control and placebo — so the count in the green box does not match the registry it is asserting over, and a reader cannot tell whether control and placebo are deliberately excluded or simply missing. Worse, the box counts entry-8pct as a healthy running arm on live_n=3 with declined=47; an arm with three live trades supplies no live-tape evidence and its presence inflates the 'arms are live' assurance. The check establishes that rows exist, not that arms are producing evidence.

findings.claim: kernel_agreement is green at '195/200 live setups reproduced (97.5%)' and the +0.59pp entry-granularity gap is declared harmless for arm-vs-arm work because 'all arms share this kernel'.
findings.problem: That shared-kernel argument does not hold for arms whose changed parameter is the pump threshold. The kernel reads pumps 0.59pp larger on average across 200 matched setups, and entry-8pct is defined by pump_pct=8.0, so the bias sits directly on that arm's admission boundary and systematically admits detections the live bot would not have taken — visible in its declined=47 against control's declined=33. The declared limitation covers absolute WR but is asserted to leave arm-vs-arm comparisons valid, and for the entry_trigger class that assertion is not established. The five misses are also concentrated in one name (four BOME, one BANANA), so the 97.5% figure is not evidence of coin-independent agreement.

findings.claim: no_lookahead is green and critical: 're-detected 108 events on truncated history across 6 coins; mismatches: none'.
findings.problem: The coverage behind that green box is a small slice of the population it certifies — 108 events against events by tier backfill=4764, and 6 coins against 176 coins in the data. Zero mismatches on that slice does not establish look-ahead freedom across the universe, particularly for the thin names this project has already identified as where the edge lives. The check also verifies detection only; the arms under test change sl_pct, tp_pct, max_hold_h and sl_anchor, all of which are exit-path logic that this probe never exercised, so an entire class of look-ahead in the exit simulation is uncovered while the box reads green and critical.
